tags.chapter_name: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision

question.text:
A balloon and its content having mass $M$ is moving up with an acceleration ' $a$ '. The mass that must be released from the content so that the balloon starts moving up with an acceleration ' $3 a^{\prime}$ will be
(Take ' g ' as acceleration due to gravity)

solution.text: $\begin{aligned} & F-m g=m a \\ & F=m a+m g \\ & F-(m-x) g=(m-x) 3 a \end{aligned}$ Put F $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{Ma}+\mathrm{mg}-\mathrm{mg}+\mathrm{xg}=3 \mathrm{ma}-3 \mathrm{xa} \\ & \mathrm{x}=\frac{2 \mathrm{ma}}{\mathrm{~g}+3 \mathrm{a}} \end{aligned}$
